articles.title: Sociologists found strict atheists aren’t the ones pairing science with ghosts and jinxes—that link appears in people straddling two worlds you’d expect to clash
articles.summary: Trusting science over church rules doesn't always erase superstition—it just shifts it away from traditional miracles. Research shows ghosts, curses, and everyday rituals resonate most with people who pair a scientific outlook with lingering ties to faith, not strict atheists.

articles.summary: Researchers followed young viewers across an entire season of Love Island to see whether feeling pressured by contestants' bodies shifts how audiences try to change their own. Their findings point to a surprising twist involving timing.

articles.title: How narcissistic employees manipulate their way to the top
articles.summary: Employees with narcissistic traits use distinct strategies to close the status gap with their bosses. A new study reveals how these workers rely on personal bonding, requests for special privileges, and workplace gossip to climb the corporate ladder.

articles.title: Even mild ADHD symptoms in adolescence are linked to later antisocial and criminal behavior, twin study finds
articles.summary: Finnish adolescents with more ADHD symptoms, even below diagnostic levels, tended to report more antisocial behavior and criminal activity in adulthood, and higher cognitive ability did not weaken the link, a twin study found.

articles.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. Existing evaluations often provide isolated theorem statements in settings where much of this supporting theory is already available in Mathlib. We introduce AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks drawn from 24 advanced mathematical sources

articles.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. articles.title: Scientists identify two ages when children may be most vulnerable to screen time
articles.summary: Scientists have identified two potentially critical periods when screen time may be especially detrimental to children's learning and memory: infancy and the start of formal schooling. Greater screen exposure during these developmental windows was linked to poorer academic performance and weaker working memory years later.

articles.title: This dietary supplement may have an unexpected benefit for the brain
articles.summary: A naturally derived dietary supplement called urolithin A may help the brain get more oxygen and nutrients when it needs them most. In a randomized clinical trial involving 50 middle-aged adults with obesity, researchers found that taking the supplement daily for four weeks increased blood flow to the brain during a challenging memory task, particularly in a region involved in working memory.

articles.title: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men
articles.summary: Men and women appear to be similarly capable of multitasking, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while juggling multiple activities. Researchers believe this unexpected difference may help explain why women are widely perceived as better multitaskers.

articles.title: For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work
articles.summary: A major new study challenges a long-standing assumption about how the brain works, revealing that most neurons are versatile multitaskers rather than highly specialized workers. By analyzing recordings from 43 regions of the mouse brain, researchers discovered that although some neurons are dedicated to specific functions, most respond to a wide variety of information in remarkably distinct ways.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
articles.summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness.

articles.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. Traditional antidepressants often work less effectively for these individuals, potentially explaining why some people struggle to find relief.
